explanation: The Capture of Bahia article closes its lead on the answer this edge names: "Although the Dutch intentions were reported to the Spanish, no preventive counter-action was taken until the Recapture of Bahia in 1625." The Recapture article opens with the same thing said from the other side: "The recapture of Bahia was a Spanish–Portuguese military expedition in 1625 to retake the city of Bahia in Brazil from the forces of the Dutch West India Company (WIC)." An expedition mounted to retake a city taken the year before is a reaction to the taking and not a consequence of it, so `reacted-to` and not `caused`. Probable, because both articles are read at one revision each and neither names a historian for the reading.
